text: The intent node states why flightcrew exists and what it is; it does not say what this second attempt must leave behind or why the first attempt's result is not it. Ten problems name the defects. The intent must say, in one sentence a stranger can act on, the outcome of this run and the reason it is worth a second run, so that the test-builder knows what the end-to-end proof exercises and the critic knows what the diff is judged against.

The system names an attempt where the work is a launch: one folder per attempt, refused for reuse, with no parent that holds the attempts of one piece of work, no count and no shared address. The spec is copied into every attempt and locked there when the record already pins it by version and commit. The interval in which a spec is made has no address the tooling knows, no command that opens it and no recorded starting point, though every spec in the repository was grown that way. The log heads each entry with a folder name, so two runs of one launch read as two unrelated things. Target model: flightdeck/launch/<name>/ holding specs/ (the version series, its interview/, the tests map) and runs/run-<n>/, with one log beside all launches. Open inside it: the exact file set at each address, whether an abandoned run's outputs are kept in place, archived or overwritten, and the run branch convention now that a run has a number (structure-problems P1-P5, P7; run-problems 1-6, 9, 12-13; launch/README.md is rewritten to the result).

The run's documents are not yet a foundation anything but the runner can read or write. Ten schemas exist, for the spec, plan, tests map, launch record, check result, event and four returns; the kickoff, the run report, the run log entry, the evidence summary and five role returns have none, so they exist only as rendered markdown or prose. One file holds two kinds of state: freeze, whether a document is immutable, is enforced through the launch record's locked-paths list, populated only when a map is pinned, so nothing is locked from launch creation to pin, a hand edit to a pinned spec copy is never reported, every guard must first resolve an active launch, and two active launches fail every command; phase, where a launch is, lives in the same file. Target: every artefact a run reads or writes is a JSON document with a schema, written by the thing that produces it, so a later local web page can read run assets directly and mutate the ones a human owns without going through a command; that page is a later spec, and this spec fixes the documents it will plug into. Freeze is written in the document's own status field and a hook refuses an edit by reading the file it is about to touch, with no knowledge of which run is active; phase is indexed in the launch record and only there, and the launch record holds nothing a workflow's arguments or a document's own field already carries. Locked paths remain a mechanism for what a status field cannot cover, a test folder, a fixture, a library a check imports, and the map has no field declaring what a check depends on, so locking the check does not lock what decides its verdict. Decide: the full set of documents, which are human-owned and mutable, which are agent-written and immutable, and what remains in the launch record once freeze and conduct leave it (fc-problems P2; testing-problems P5; kickoff-problems P4; crew-problems P3).

The runner became the control surface. No source names a runner; the build collapsed every artefact, the kickoff, the plan, the dispatches, the evidence, the report and the log stub, behind one entry of 19 commands in 44 forms, two thirds of the system by line count. The human advances a run by typing fifteen commands where the sources have the human read a display and approve at a gate. The frozen v1 spec describes that program: 57 of 78 behaviours name the runner and interface I1 is its command surface, so the tests test the CLI and the critics judged its fidelity to itself. Its own one-line output rule is broken by eight commands, the evidence render swallows errors, and the shim invokes a bare node. Decide: the fate of fc itself, kept under its name, renamed, or dissolved into scripts each called by path; which built commands survive as leaf commands that take paths, write one artefact and work alone (check, boundary and locked folded together, the three renders, evidence, report, log stub, plan render, return, validate, lint, budget, worker merge); that the eleven launch state subcommands are not leaves and that no command a human types advances a run; whether any new leaf is needed, in particular one that opens a launch folder from an idea and one that opens a numbered run under it, since nothing today creates either; and the spec seam: a node about an artefact's state, a hook's enforcement, a role's inputs and outputs or a rendering's contents stays; a node about arguments, resolution order, exit codes or which subcommand does what is implementation and leaves. The four manuals written as command sequences are rewritten to that seam (fc-problems P1, P3, P4, P5; system-problems P9; run-problems 12-13; v1 decisions D2, D15, D16 reopened).

Conduct became commands. The kickoff base's twelve content lines are eight runner commands; the sources' base carries gates, escalation rules and evidence requirements with no command in it. The sources place the kickoff and the dynamic workflow side by side as one thing seen from two sides, the readable statement of conduct and its executable form, and never draw the seam between them; the built system resolved it by moving every deterministic step into the runner. The three shipped workflow scripts have never run, cannot pass their own locked syntax check and execute in the runtime at once, and the kickoff module that selects them contradicts the base. Every other document a run consumes has a schema; the kickoff has none, so no page can read it, no script can refuse it and no check can compare it across runs. Its version string is recorded in three places and verified against nothing while the library moved from one to three underneath it. Its numbers have no single owner: ceilings in the launch record, model tiers in the plan and crew README, gate reading stated twice. The runtime offers what neither the kickoff nor the runner built: a saved script that owns the order of stages and the fan-out, receives its variables as JSON arguments, predetermines which agent runs at each stage, dictates each return's shape by schema, cannot be stopped early by the agents inside it, and ends where a human must decide, so that a phase is a prebuilt workflow started after a gate and the gate is where the workflow ends. Under that shape most of the state the launch record holds and most of the commands the orchestrator types are absorbed by the script and its arguments. Decide: whether a run's phases are prebuilt workflows kicked off after each gate, and what the kickoff still says once they are; whether the kickoff's structured form is the arguments those workflows take, with a schema as its version and compatibility check; which values survive the routing test as conduct (gates, dispatch rules, default budgets, model tiers, review policy, ending policy) and which move to the spec, plan, role files and settings; which script ending the runtime requires, recorded where the next author reads; whether the task module for agent-shaped work is carried forward (kickoff-problems P1-P4, P6; system-problems P7, P8; fc-problems P2, P4).

The testing vocabulary is defined in five places that disagree, carries two class axes under near-identical names in every map, and has no word for a project's own test or for the wrapper that adapts one to a run. The manuals define three verdicts a check may return, an exit code, a ratio against a pre-stated threshold, and a verdict sheet against a rubric; the built system records one, derived from the exit code alone, and the map, the result schema, the gates and the test-builder's procedure know nothing of the other two, so any agent-shaped behaviour tagged statistical or judged ends as unverified. Checks have no home: four documents send them to four places and none is the run; the test-builder receives no run, hardcodes a spec folder no command creates, and sends new checks first into the project's own tests, the one place a run must never write. The testbench harness rule, the untestable vocabulary and the class obligations sit where the builder never reads. Target rail, in placement order: the project's own tests folder first (assertive tests in the project's own framework, owned by the project); flightdeck/testbench/ where a test does not suit the project folder (fixtures, benches, harnesses); launch/<name>/runs/run-<n>/checks/ for the wrappers the map names, written after the freeze and before implementation; flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/ for the libraries and gates every launch shares. That last folder's name collides with the run's checks folder while holding nothing a map names as a check, and a rename to verify is the leaning. Decide: what a statistical and a judged check look like on disk, what command produces each, what file the ratio or sheet lands in and how a gate reads it; where the tests map lives given its version series assumes one folder beside the spec while the checks it names live in the run; whether a run-local wrapper is a script or only a command string; the shared folder's name (testing-problems P1-P4, P6, P7; the three testing manuals and terms.md are aligned to the result).

The constitution names fourteen roles, the guides seven, the built system ten. Four the constitution names do not exist: the interface builder that halts on a spec-codebase contradiction rather than iterating to green at the seams, the strong worker that retries a failed unit once on a stronger tier from a clean state before a human is asked, the per-unit adversary that attacks a completed unit before merge, and the scribe whose absence leaves a failed report render unnoticed. Without a tier below it the implementer runs on the strongest model for every unit and a red unit has one outcome. The test-builder is a session in practice and a subagent on paper, with a turn budget, an accept-edits mode, a described dispatch it never receives and no tool to ask the human; the spec-builder is a session agent because it holds the ask-user tool, and nothing says so. A role's reach is declared in two files that never reconcile, the frontmatter and the permission fragment, so the fragment denies the very path the test-builder is told to write; against the constitution's six frontmatter fields most roles declare one, the orchestrator's model is inherit, no role declares hooks or memory. Decide: which of the four missing hats are roles, kickoff rules or workflow stages; whether the test-builder is a session agent or a dispatched subagent; which file declares a role's reach or how the two are reconciled; whether any hook is scoped to a role; whether the spec chain stays byte-frozen for calibration or follows the rules every other role file follows (crew-problems P1, P5; system-problems P6).

Dispatch is sealed for three roles and freehand for four. The implementer, critic and verifier receive a rendered prompt from a template; the explorer has a template no command renders; the planner, spec-judge and spec-attacker have neither, so whoever spawns them composes the prompt and nothing records what they were handed or guards what they must not see. Three roles enumerate in their own body what a dispatch always names and nothing honours it. Half the returns have no shape: worker, explorer, verifier and critic return against a schema a command stores; the test-builder's, orchestrator's, spec-builder's, judge's and attacker's are prose, while the crew manual states handoffs travel through schemas as a universal rule. Six roles are told things their tools or dispatch contradict: the critic checks path globs its dispatch never carries, the orchestrator runs an escalate form the runner refuses, the verifier must not write and rewrites three files, the planner is asked for files it cannot write, the attacker is told to run commands with no tool to, the implementer's check invocation contradicts the design contract. The orchestrator's method names eighteen runner commands, has no procedure for the targets stage and no render for a fix dispatch. Target: every subagent receives a sealed dispatch rendered from agent file, project template and per-unit fill; every return consumed downstream has a schema validated at the handoff; every human-started role has a recorded invocation; a role file names nothing its tools or its dispatch cannot supply (crew-problems P2, P3, P4, P6).

The guards intercept Edit, Write and NotebookEdit and nothing intercepts Bash, which nine of ten roles hold, so a locked file is locked by instruction; the sandbox deny list that would reach the shell ships as an example, and the allow list grants git add, commit and switch to every role and makes every workflow model-invocable. Every hook runs through a wrapper that catches every error and exits zero, so a guard that crashes permits what it was about to refuse; the stop gate exits zero when no map is pinned or the file is unreadable, indistinguishable from green; it runs in two phases of seven and not in implement, the phase with general write access; its eighth-block stall goes to stderr, which the session never displays, after which every edit is silently denied. Two structural checks exist, one wired with no timeout and one with a timeout wired to nothing. The manifest's header says every new file belongs on a line and nothing walks the tree to assert it. Target: every guarantee a run relies on is enforced by something that does not consult the agent; a hook that cannot decide refuses rather than permits; a gate exists in every phase a role can write in; a stall is visible to the session it stalls; irreversible actions are denied and side-effecting workflows are human-invoked only. Decide whether Bash is sandboxed and by which of the inactive mechanisms (system-problems P4, P5, P11).

The end command records an ending and performs none of it: it writes outcome, status and phase, renders the report and the log stub, prints the worktrees to remove and the branches to delete, and removes nothing, deletes nothing, prunes nothing; the branch names it prints are synthesised from the plan without asking git. Gate three, the human's final reading of the evidence, has no source phase, no destination and no blocker; the end command never reads the gates object, so both recorded runs ended with the final gate pending and an outcome set. The land command checks the evidence summary at a commit the human names and cannot tell a rebased integration branch from the pre-rebase state; the integration branch, the rebase, the rerun proof, the pull request, CI and one commit per unit are all the human's hand steps, and the cost line the merge gate requires reads not recorded everywhere. After an abandoned run everything remains and the salvage table, setup carries and output does not, is enforced by no code; the archive folder the deck reserved has never been written. The record contradicts itself: partial belongs to both outcome families, at-stage is free text, optional lines are always emitted, the log's preamble sits beneath its entries. Decide: whether an abandoned run's branch is kept for its evidence or deleted, since the guides disagree and the system chose by making no branch; which of the merge gate's three conditions the system records; how many outcome words there are for three endings (endings-problems P1, P2, P5, P6, P7; structure-problems P4).

The human's diagnosis has no enforcement twin and never reaches the next run. The log stub reserves five fill fields for the human and nothing refuses while a marker remains, nothing refuses an agent that writes them, and the next launch opens without reading the log; both real entries carry draft (orchestrator) on every judgement field and nothing objected. The retry carries a filename: the previous-launch field is a name, the kickoff header points at the log and the render never opens it, so two rendered kickoffs of the same spec are byte-identical and the failure reaches the next plan only if an agent chooses to write a risk, whose heading reference warns and never errors. The manual's retry rules, one change per retry named by the watch field, same spec and kickoff except the edit, demote when no wave was parallel, shelve after three failures on one axis, are compared by nothing. The tests map was revised mid-run by the orchestrator where the manual says an agent reports and stops and a human decides the revision after the log is written. Target: an agent never writes a fill field and the system refuses if it does; the next run does not open while the previous entry stands unfilled; the previous entry's diagnosis reaches the next kickoff as content, not a pointer; a retry differs from the last run by one attributable change and the record can show which; no map is edited inside a run (endings-problems P3, P4; kickoff-problems P5; structure-problems P5).
The intent text was composed from four free-text answers; the provider has not read the assembled sentence.

v1 carried eighteen decisions. Ten of the registered problems reopen at least eight of them by name (D2 one entry point, D3 active launch by status, D4 spec chain byte-frozen, D9 stop-gate phases, D15 orchestrator writes through commands, D16 no scribe, D18 pinned copies, D10 no judge runner). Which survive, which are retired now and which are re-decided at their own domain has to be settled before scope is drawn.

The tempting expansions this run must not make are unstated: the local web control surface the JSON foundation exists for, the migration of folders on other branches, CI, edits to the spec schema and rubric corpus, and the two build scripts under .claude/workflows/ that the boundary reported and nobody decided.

The testbench is 12,927 lines and 30 green suites, more than half of them exercising the runner's command surface. Under the seam the runner leaves the spec, so the suites that test it lose their spec node. What becomes of them decides how much of the green record survives this run.

The provider asked to rename the pilot agent to scout. pilot names a plan-unit flag (the units a wave runs first), not a role; nothing in the tree calls a role pilot. Whether the flag is renamed, or a role is meant, is the provider's to say.

Where a role's reach is declared — frontmatter as the single source with the settings allow list derived, or two hand-maintained files with a check — is unsettled and the provider asked for exploration. X14 reports frontmatter carries tools, disallowedTools, permissionMode, isolation, hooks, memory, skills; whether an agent's frontmatter hooks run only while that agent acts is probable, not certain.

The provider says most single-artefact commands can be absorbed by hooks, workflows and frontmatter and asks for investigation. Which of check, evidence, report, log stub, return, events append, budget and worker merge a hook or workflow can carry natively, given X14's facts on what SubagentStop, Stop, PostToolUse and SessionEnd receive, decides which leaves remain.
